title: United Nations · Universal Declaration of Human Rights
summary: Dignity, equal rights, life and freedom from cruelty provide a public baseline for reviewing conduct. Assess acts and consequences without assigning guilt through identity.

title: UNICEF · Core Commitments for Children
summary: A humanitarian framework for meeting children’s needs and protecting them during emergencies. Use vulnerability and concrete needs when comparing proposed provision.

title: World Food Programme · Ethical culture
summary: Humanity, impartiality, neutrality and operational independence guide humanitarian action. Assistance is evaluated through need and conduct rather than prestige or group membership.

title: WOAH · Animal welfare
summary: Animal welfare concerns living conditions, nourishment, health, behaviour and relief from fear and suffering. Include animal needs and dependencies in constructive-action reviews.

title: ICRC · Conduct of hostilities and protection of civilians
summary: The conduct of armed conflict is constrained by civilian protection, distinction, proportionality and precautions. Claimed good intentions do not erase the consequences of cruelty or indiscriminate harm.
